question.worked_solution:
To remove the radical $\sqrt{7}$ from the denominator, all we need to do is multiply both the numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{7}$ and simplify:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\sqrt{7}}\cdot \frac{\sqrt{7}}{\sqrt{7}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{7}}{(\sqrt{7})^{2}} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{7}}{7} & \end{aligned}
$$

Now, we use the product rule to simplify the numerator:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\sqrt{3}\cdot \sqrt{7}}{7} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{3\cdot 7}}{7} & = \\ \frac{\sqrt{21}}{7} & \end{aligned}
$$
